It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former shrine Rank under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Shrine Rank}} was {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326}}{{efn|lt=Fu-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917326|qq= 近代社格制度}}. It belongs to the {{ill|Izumi Province|en|Izumi Province|qid=Q1047117|lt=Izumi Province}} and the {{ill|Ichinomiya|en|Ichinomiya|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}, and is also known as “Shinoda Myōjin”, “Shinoda Shrine”, and “Shinoda Seishinja” among other names.

== 祭神 ==
* {{ill|Hijiri no Ōkami|qid=Q135524506}} (ひじりのおおかみ)  
  {{ill|Hijiri no Ōkami|qid=Q135524506}} appears in the {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} as the child deity ({{ill|Child Deity|de|Mikokami|ja|御子神|zh|御子神|qid=Q352176}}) of the {{ill|Toshigami|ja|大年神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Great Age Deity|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to QID FIXED|qid=Q3028663|comment=changed title based on wikidata}}. According to the “Origin of the Great Deities of the Five Shrines of Izumi Province and the Main Shrine of Fuchū” the {{ill|Honji suijaku|en|Honji suijaku|qid=Q3080781|lt=Honji Buddha}} is regarded as {{ill|Kṣitigarbha|en|Kṣitigarbha|qid=Q604687|lt=Jizō Bodhisattva}}.

== History ==
[[File:Hijiri-jinja (Izumi, Osaka) honden2.jpg|180px|thumb|Main Hall]]
In the tradition of this shrine, there are two legends. One, noted in a ’s eastern expedition, {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|en|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q1056017|lt=Ninigi no Mikoto}} was enshrined here.|date=May 2023}}, and the other, which states that on August 15 of the 3rd year of {{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|ru|Хакухо|zh|白鳳|qid=Q11580612}} ({{ill|675|ab|675|af|675|am|675 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|675|ar|675|ary|675|arz|675|ast|675|az|675|azb|۶۷۵ (میلادی)|be|675|be_x_old|675|bg|675|bn|৬৭৫|bpy|মারি ৬৭৫|br|675|bs|675.|ca|675|cdo|675 nièng|ceb|675|ckb|٦٧٥|crh|675|cs|675|cv|675|cy|675|da|675|de|675|el|675|eml|675|eo|675|es|675|et|675|eu|675|fa|۶۷۵ (میلادی)|fi|675|fo|675|fr|675|fy|675|ga|675|gan|675年|gd|675|gl|675|he|675|hi|675|hr|675.|ht|675 (almanak jilyen)|hu|675|hy|675|id|675|io|675|it|675|ja|675年|jv|675|ka|675|kk|675 жыл|ko|675년|la|675|lb|675|lij|675|lmo|675|lt|675 m.|map_bms|675|mdf|675|mg|675|mhr|675|mk|675|mr|इ.स. ६७५|mrj|675 и|ms|675|mzn|۶۷۵|nah|675|nap|675|nds|675|nds_nl|675|new|सन् ६७५|nl|675|nn|675|no|675|nrm|675|nso|675|oc|675|or|୬୭୫|os|675-æм аз|pl|675|pnb|675|pt|675|qu|675|ro|675|ru|675 год|rue|675|sa|६७५|scn|675|sd|675ع|se|675|sh|675.|shn|675|si|675|simple|675|sk|675|sl|675|sq|675|sr|675|su|675|sv|675|sw|675|tg|Соли 675|th|พ.ศ. 1218|tk|675|tl|675|tly|675|tr|675|tt|675 ел|uk|675|ur|675ء|uz|675|vec|675|vi|675|war|675|wuu|675年|xmf|675|zh|675年|zh_min_nan|675 nî|zh_yue|675年|qid=Q30523|lt=675 AD}}), by imperial command of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|en|Emperor Tenmu|qid=Q335181|lt=Emperor Tenmu}}, Shinoda leader (しのだのおびと) of the immigrant ({{ill|Toraijin|en|Toraijin|qid=Q11561926|lt=Immigrant}}) clan ({{ill|Clan|en|Clan|qid=Q211503|lt=Clan}}) enshrined the {{ill|Hijiri no Ōkami|qid=Q135524506}}.  
On May 7 of the 1st year of the {{ill|Jōgan|en|Jōgan|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} era ({{ill|859|en|859|qid=Q23897|lt=859 AD}}), it was designated as a {{ill|kokuheisha|ja|官社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Government Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 官幣社|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11452104}}, and on August 13 of the same year, it received the shrine Rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|en|Shinkai (divine rank)|qid=Q11591025|lt=Shrine Rank}}) from the 5th Rank below to the 4th Rank below (as recorded in the {{ill|Sandaijitsuroku|ja|三代実録}}). In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (日本)|lt=Enchō|lt_ja=延長|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Enchō|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 延長 (元号)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1327274}} ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470|lt=927 AD}}), the “Divine Name Register” ({{ill|Engishiki Divine Name Register|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Divine Name Register}}) compiled under the {{ill|Engishiki|en|Engishiki|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}} lists it ({{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|lt=Shikinaisha}}). In the medieval “Izumi Province Divine Name Register” ({{ill|Izumi Province Divine Name Register|ja|国内神名帳|lt=Izumi Province Divine Name Register|lt_ja=和泉国神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumi Province Divine Name Register|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11420490}}), the shrine Rank is recorded as “First Rank.”

During the {{ill|Kamakura period|en|Kamakura period|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, the Shinoda clan served as hereditary priests, but in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|en|Nanboku-chō period|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}, after siding with the {{ill|Southern Court|en|Southern Court|qid=Q3001082|lt=Southern Court}}, they lost their priestly status; and in the 5th year of {{ill|Enbun|en|Enbun|qid=Q1145071|lt=Enbun}} ({{ill|1360|en|1360|qid=Q6150|lt=1360 AD}}) the position was taken over by Wada Kurando. From the Nanboku-chō period onward, along with other shrines in {{ill|Izumi Province|en|Izumi Province|qid=Q1047117|lt=Izumi Province}} such as {{ill|Ōtori taisha|en|Ōtori taisha|qid=Q705151|lt=Ōtori Taisha}}, {{ill|Izumianashi Shrine|ja|泉穴師神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumanaishi Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11554908}}, {{ill|Tsugawa Shrine|ja|積川神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsugikawa Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11597137}}, and {{ill|Hine Shrine|ja|日根神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hine Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11509543}}, it came to be known as one of the “Five Great Shrines.” Although it occupies the third Rank of shrines in Izumi Province, the term “Sannomiya” does not appear in medieval records.

In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|en|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō Era}} ({{ill|1575|en|1575|qid=Q6688|lt=1575 AD}}), it was granted 1,100 {{ill|Koku|en|Koku|qid=Q855048|lt=stone}} as its domain by {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|en|Oda Nobunaga|qid=Q171411|lt=Oda Nobunaga}}, but in the 13th year ({{ill|1585|en|1585|qid=Q6736|lt=1585 AD}}) during {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|en|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|qid=Q187550|lt=Toyotomi Hideyoshi}}’s {{ill|Battle of Kishuu|ja|紀州征伐#和泉の戦い|lt=Negoro Attack|lt_ja=根来攻め|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kishū Expedition|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10855721}}, the shrine suffered damage from warfare and its holdings were confiscated.

In the early {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}, Toyotomi Hideyori appointed {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|en|Katagiri Katsumoto|qid=Q1882775|lt=Katagiri Katsumoto}} as commissioner to construct and repair shrines and temples throughout the region, and this shrine was rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} ({{ill|1604|en|1604|qid=Q6738|lt=1604 AD}}). The existing structures from that time—the main hall and the sub-shrines of the three shrines, the waterfall shrine, and the Hiraoka shrine—have been designated as {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}} and as {{ill|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Tangible Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q2901860|lt=Tangible Cultural Property}} of {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Osaka|af|Osaka-prefektuur|an|Prefectura d'Osaka|ang|Ōsacascir|ar|أوساكا (محافظة)|arz|محافظة Prefecture}}. In addition, there was a {{ill|Jingū-ji|en|Jingū-ji|qid=Q1074971|lt=Jingū-ji}} affiliated with {{ill|Shingon Buddhism|en|Shingon Buddhism|qid=Q550182|lt=Shingon Buddhism}}’s Manshōin, which featured a {{ill|Five-storied Pagoda|ja|五重塔}} and a Bell Hall (鐘堂). In the 8th year of {{ill|Kansei|en|Kansei|qid=Q1195131|lt=Kansei}} ({{ill|1796|en|1796|qid=Q7818|lt=1796 AD}}), a dispute arose between the shrine family ({{ill|Shake (social class)|en|Shake (social class)|qid=Q11588367|lt=Shrine family}}) and the shrine priest ({{ill|Shrine Priest|ja|社僧}}).

With the advent of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, the separation of Shinto and Buddhism ({{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|ca|Shinbutsu bunri|de|Shinbutsu-Bunri|es|Shinbutsu bunri|fa|شینبوتسو بونری|fi|Shinbutsu bunri|fr|Shinbutsu bunri|id|Shinbutsu bunri|it|Shinbutsu bunri|ja|神仏分離|ru|Симбуцу бунри|tr|Şinbutsu-bunri|zh|神佛分離|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu Bunri}}) led to the closure of the Manshōin at the Jingū-ji. In {{ill|1872|en|1872|qid=Q7753|lt=1872 AD}} (5th year of Meiji), it was Ranked as a local shrine, and in March {{ill|1943|en|1943|qid=Q18623|lt=1943 AD}} (18th year of {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|qid=Q327567|lt=Shōwa}}) it was elevated to {{ill|Fu-sha|qid=Q134917326}}{{efn|lt=Fu-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917326|qq= 近代社格制度}} status.

The “Chū Izumi Kaidō”, which stretches from Yosumatsu-cho in {{ill|Izumiōtsu|en|Izumiōtsu|qid=Q873553|lt=Izumiotsu City}}, is also known as the “Nunobiki Road”. It is said that when Shinoda Daimyōjin landed at Yosumatsu-hama, he drew cloth as he proceeded toward Hijiri Shrine. A monument commemorating the “Chū Izumi Kaidō” stands at its intersection with the {{ill|Kishū Kaidō|ja|紀州街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kishū Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11605050}}.

== Shrine Grounds ==
[[File:Hijiri-jinja (Izumi, Osaka) honden1.jpg|180px|thumb|Main Hall (Important Cultural Property)]]
[[File:Hijiri-jinja (Izumi, Osaka) Taki-jinja+San-jinja.jpg|180px|thumb|Sub-shrine of the Three Shrines (right) and the Waterfall Shrine (left); both are Important Cultural Properties]]
[[File:Hijiri-jinja (Izumi, Osaka) Hiraoka-jinja honden.jpg|180px|thumb|Main Hall of the Hiraoka Shrine (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Osaka Prefecture)]]
* Main Hall ({{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Property}}) – Rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} ({{ill|1604|en|1604|qid=Q6738|lt=1604 AD}}) by Toyotomi Hideyori with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|en|Katagiri Katsumoto|qid=Q1882775|lt=Katagiri Katsumoto}} as commissioner. The shrine structure is built in the {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|en|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|qid=Q855025|lt=Irimoya-zukuri}} style with {{ill|cypress bark roof|ja|檜皮葺|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Cypress Bark Roofing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q90373477}}, featuring a front decoration of {{ill|Bargeboard|ja|千鳥破風|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Chidori-hafū|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 破風|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q4881511}} and a one-kan eave of {{ill|Karahafu|en|Karahafu|qid=Q977293|lt=Karahafū}} on the {{ill|kōhai|ja|向拝|2=ja|3=向拝|4=zh|5=向拜|lt=kōhai|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukaehai|13=User:Immanuelle/kōhai (architecture)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11415970}}. It was designated a Specially Protected Building on April 15, {{ill|1924|en|1924|qid=Q2173|lt=1924 AD}} (13th year of {{ill|Taishō era|en|Taishō era|qid=Q329174|lt=Taishō}}) under the {{ill|Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law|ja|古社寺保存法|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ancient Shrines and Temples Preservation Law|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11411552}}, and became an Important Cultural Property with the enforcement of the {{ill|Cultural Properties Protection Law|ja|文化財保護法}} in {{ill|1950|en|1950|qid=Q18597|lt=1950 AD}}.
* Worship Hall
* Shrine Office
* {{ill|Acala|en|Acala|qid=Q337624|lt=Fudō Myōō}} – A remnant of {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu Shūgō}}.
* Remote Worship Site – A modern structure modeled after the remote worship site of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}}.

=== Auxiliary and Subshrines ===
* Three Shrines (Important Cultural Property) – Rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} ({{ill|1604|en|1604|qid=Q6738|lt=1604 AD}}) by Toyotomi Hideyori with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|en|Katagiri Katsumoto|qid=Q1882775|lt=Katagiri Katsumoto}} as commissioner. Its brilliant colors and ornate decorations exemplify the characteristics of the {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|ja|桃山時代|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Momoyama period|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 安土桃山時代|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q319531}}. The shrine structure is built in the three-kan style in the {{ill|Kasuga-zukuri|en|Kasuga-zukuri|qid=Q3193781|lt=Kasuga-zukuri}} with Cypress Bark Roofing; the three-kan style (with three bays at the front) of the Kasuga-zukuri is rare nationwide. It was relocated to its present site in {{ill|1873|en|1873|qid=Q7757|lt=1873 AD}} (6th year of Meiji).
* Waterfall Shrine (Important Cultural Property) – Also rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} ({{ill|1604|en|1604|qid=Q6738|lt=1604 AD}}) by Toyotomi Hideyori with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|en|Katagiri Katsumoto|qid=Q1882775|lt=Katagiri Katsumoto}} as commissioner. The shrine structure is a one-kan building in the Kasuga-zukuri style with Cypress Bark Roofing, and its Mukaehai is formed with a eave of Karahafū. It was relocated to its present site in {{ill|1873|en|1873|qid=Q7757|lt=1873 AD}} (6th year of Meiji).
* Hiraoka Shrine (Tangible Cultural Property designated by Osaka Prefecture) – Rebuilt in the 9th year of {{ill|Keichō|en|Keichō|qid=Q1328185|lt=Keichō}} ({{ill|1604|en|1604|qid=Q6738|lt=1604 AD}}) by Toyotomi Hideyori with {{ill|Katagiri Katsumoto|en|Katagiri Katsumoto|qid=Q1882775|lt=Katagiri Katsumoto}} as commissioner. The main hall is a one-kan building in the Kasuga-zukuri style with Cypress Bark Roofing.
* Kotohira Shrine – Enshrines the deity {{ill|Ōmononushi|en|Ōmononushi|qid=Q10936701|qid=Q10936701|lt=Ōmononushi}}.
* Itsukushima Shrine – Enshrines the deity {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|lt=Ichikishima-hime}}.
* Inari Mounds – Numerous mounds enshrine the deity {{ill|Inari Ōkami|en|Inari Ōkami|qid=Q719665|lt=Inari Ōkami}}.

== Transportation ==
* Get off at {{ill|West Japan Railway Company|en|West Japan Railway Company|qid=Q502125|lt=JR}} on the {{ill|Hanwa Line|en|Hanwa Line|qid=Q1154800|lt=Hanwa Line}} at {{ill|Kita-Shinoda Station|en|Kita-Shinoda Station|qid=Q856975|lt=Kitashinoda Station}}.

== 周囲 ==
* {{ill|Kumano Kaidō|ja|熊野街道|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kumano Kaidō|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11568976}} – The shrine’s {{ill|Torii|en|Torii|qid=Q234731|lt=Torii Gate}} and {{ill|Komainu|en|Komainu|qid=Q20155846|lt=Komainu}} stand along the Kumano Kaidō.
* {{ill|Shinoda Ōji Shrine|ja|篠田王子|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoda Ōji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11603815}}
* {{ill|Shinodanomori Kuzunoha Inari Shrine|ja|信太森葛葉稲荷神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinoda Mori Katsuwa Inari Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11386029}}
* {{ill|Furufu Shrine|ja|舊府神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Old Furu Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11613492}} (ふるふじんじゃ) – Enshrines a white fox “bakeishi.”
* Shinoda no Mori Furusato-kan & Shinoda no Mori Kagamiike Historic Park – When walking from the shrine toward Kagamiike, one encounters “Nezumi-zaka,” a slope said to be where the father of {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|Abe no Seimei|qid=Q1150151|lt=Abe no Seimei}}, {{ill|Abe no Yasuna|ja|安倍保名}}, met his wife {{ill|Kuzunoha|en|Kuzunoha|qid=Q1651785|lt=Kuzunoha}}.
* {{ill|Inryō-ji|ja|蔭凉寺 (和泉市)|lt=Inryō-ji}}
* {{ill|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|en|Izumi Koganezuka Kofun|qid=Q11417846|lt=Izumi Koganezuka Kofun}}
